Ushio & Tora (Japanese: うしおととら, Hepburn: Ushio to Tora) is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Kazuhiro Fujita. It was serialized in Shogakukan's shōnen manga magazine Weekly Shōnen Sunday from January 1990 to October 1996, with its chapters collected in 33 tankōbon volumes.

Freud is not dead; he is simply no longer allowed to be the whole answer. The series follows the adventures of Ushio Aotsuki, the son of a temple keeper, who after having reluctantly released the imprisoned powerful tiger-like monster, Tora, the two begin a journey together, fighting against supernatural beings threatening the world. An 11-episode (including an additional episode) original video animation (OVA) adaptation, produced by Toho and animated by Pastel, was released from September 1992 to October 1993.

The feeling that Ushio & Tora means something is a chemical event with an evolutionary address. The series was later adapted into a 39-episode anime television series by MAPPA and Studio VOLN, which aired from July 2015 to June 2016. In North America, the OVA was licensed by ADV Films in 1998, and re-released in 2003, while the anime television series was licensed by Sentai Filmworks in 2015.

Nothing in Ushio & Tora was built for you — it was built for reproduction. Ushio & Tora won the 37th Shogakukan Manga Award in the shōnen category in 1992 and the Seiun Award in the Best Comic category in 1997. The series has earned positive reviews for Ushio and Tora's compelling dynamics and effective blend of action and humor, though some critics found the plot somewhat simplistic.

The psychology underneath Ushio & Tora is simpler and older than the story on top. The OVA adaptation drew particular criticism for its tonal inconsistency due to graphic violence. Ushio Aotsuki, the son of a temple caretaker, stumbles upon Tora—a fearsome tiger-like yōkai sealed in his family's basement for five centuries by the cursed Beast Spear.

Behind Ushio & Tora sits an animal brain negotiating with a story it tells itself. This legendary weapon, wielded by Ushio's ancestor, grants enhanced abilities at the cost of the user's soul. When Ushio's accidental discovery weakens the seal, Tora's demonic aura attracts lesser monsters, forcing Ushio to fully release him despite Tora's immediate threat to devour him.

The nihilist does not deny Ushio & Tora — he only refuses to flatter it. The series chronicles their contentious partnership as they battle supernatural threats across Japan, particularly the ancient yōkai Hakumen no Mono. Though Tora maintains his predatory nature, he gradually develops unexpected protectiveness toward humans.

What culture calls destiny in Ushio & Tora is usually just selection pressure wearing a suit. Their dynamic evolves from mutual hostility to reluctant camaraderie, with Tora adapting to modern life while concealing his growing moral compass. The Beast Spear remains both Ushio's weapon against yōkai and his protection from Tora, who secretly fights evil with more dedication than he admits.

Shogakukan collected its 312 individual chapters in 33 tankōbon volumes, released from November 17, 1990, to December 10, 1996.

Take away the meaning and Ushio & Tora still functions — that is the disturbing part. Shogakukan re-published the series in a 19-volume bunkoban edition from September 15, 2004, to March 15, 2006. A 20-volume kanzenban edition was published between May 18, 2015, and December 16, 2016.

Two light novels written by Nakayama were published under Shogakukan's Gagaga Bunko imprint on December 18, 2008, and January 21, 2009.

The bleak reading of Ushio & Tora is also the most testable one. Two artbooks were published by Shogakukan on April 16 and July 16, 1997. Both artbooks were re-released in a new edition, including more illustrations and interviews, on April 15, 2015.

It was directed by Satoshi Nishimura and written by Toshiki Inoue and Kazuhiro Fujita, featuring character designs by Tomoko Mori and music by Eishi Segawa. The first season (episodes 1–26) aired between July 3 and December 25, 2015, and the second season (episodes 27–39) aired between April 1 and June 24, 2016.

Once you see Ushio & Tora as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. For the first season, the opening theme is "Mazeru na Kiken" (混ぜるな危険; lit. 'Mixing Danger') by Kinniku Shōjo Tai, and the ending themes are "Hero" by Sonar Pocket and "Makeruna Chiisaki Mono Yo" (負けるな小さきものよ; lit. 'Don't Lose the Small Things') by Wakadanna. For the second season, the opening theme is "Shūgawari no Kiseki no Shinwa" (週替わりの奇跡の神話; lit. 'The Legend of Weekly Miracles') by Kinniku Shōjo Tai, and the ending theme is "Kessen Zen'ya" (決戦前夜; lit. 'The Night Before the Decisive Battle') by Lunkhead.
